budgets.label: Record navigation
budgets.target: Immediate local filter, selection, and row-to-detail movement on loaded records.
budgets.baseline: Obsidian-like command speed for the operator path.
budgets.detail: Atlas Studio keeps the active working set in memory and focuses records locally; cloud reads refresh the state without blocking inspection.

budgets.label: Direct record URLs
budgets.target: Every important topology record, Atlas node, operating slice, readiness item, and diagnostic has a durable address.
budgets.detail: Substrate serves stable HTTP JSON endpoints for direct object review before loading the surrounding map.

budgets.label: Viewport rendering
budgets.target: Pan and zoom reads stay bounded to the visible Atlas window and node budget.
budgets.baseline: Obsidian-like movement on large mapped workflows.
budgets.detail: The Atlas viewport endpoint returns only visible nodes, visible-node edges, LOD metadata, and omission counts so the UI can avoid reprocessing the full canvas during navigation.

budgets.label: Agent read path
budgets.target: Agents inspect the same topology, diagnostics, performance, and readiness records through API/MCP.
budgets.baseline: No UI scraping or prompt-only state.
budgets.detail: MCP resources, MCP tools, and agent commands are generated from the same management surface as the HTTP API.

budgets.label: Proof refresh
budgets.target: Receipts, diagnostics, and audit entries move as small state payloads.
budgets.baseline: Fast notes app feel with shared database durability.
budgets.detail: The Cloudflare-compatible edge adapter uses short read caching and no-store writes so inspection stays fast while mutation remains explicit.

fastPath.mechanism: Generated management resources and operations are materialized before the Worker starts.
Topology records are addressable by record id, Atlas node id, or stable slug.
Atlas pan/zoom reads can request a bounded viewport instead of loading the full session graph.
Successful GET responses carry a short public cache header; approval-gated writes use no-store.
MCP resource, MCP tool, and agent command reads all dispatch to the same in-memory API state.
Atlas Studio filters, selects, and focuses loaded nodes locally instead of waiting on graph reloads.

nonGoals: This contract does not claim production latency measurements until deployed Cloudflare telemetry is attached.
This contract does not replace D1, R2, KV, or Durable Object design decisions for a future write store.
This contract does not permit mutation without the existing approval-gated operation boundary.
